platform_sync.comment_channel_incident: the FIRST comment attempt (04:58:33Z) went through 'npx tsx' and arrived TRUNCATED to its first 79 characters: npx is npx.cmd, a batch layer that cuts a multi-line argument at the first newline. The retry invoked the same scripts/platform.ts through node + node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs, which passes the payload as one argv element and arrived whole. The truncated comment could not be deleted (the CLI exposes no comment-delete verb and the forbidden-list bars direct API calls), so issue #98 carries both comments and the LATEST one is the complete text - disclosed rather than silently re-synced. A third comment (05:04:14Z, 1395 chars, read back MATCH) is a disclosure addendum making the orphan visible on the issue itself; issue #98 therefore carries three comments and the addendum names which one is authoritative.

deviations_disclosed: RENDER-LOG GAP: the survey-era card asked for Render build/migration logs. No Render API token exists in .env (only PLATFORM/API_TOKEN/REPO_ID/MAX_SLOTS) and the GitHub token downloads GitHub job logs only, so those log bodies are NOT capturable from this environment. Rather than a BLOCKER (the card's core value - a real run id and its log line - IS satisfiable), the ACs premise on what is verifiable (GitHub run/job metadata + the committed banked job log + the live health endpoint) and make the gap an explicit named limitation: ac5 REQUIRES render_log_gap{captured:false, reason} and REDs any asserted Render log body.

scripts/platform.ts has NO actions/runs resource, so the live platform re-read (ac2) uses curl against api.github.com directly. That is a READ deviation from the issues-tracker-only channel; every issue-tracker WRITE still went through scripts/platform.ts.

Unauthenticated api.github.com reads share a 60/hour pool that this environment had EXHAUSTED mid-groom (measured remaining=0), which briefly turned ac2 RED. The probe now authenticates GitHub reads with the repo's own .env API_TOKEN - the same credential scripts/platform.ts uses and the one that downloaded the banked log - and never prints it (verified: zero token bytes in probe output). A missing or spent credential is a LOUD RED.

The banked log contains the mandated string TWICE - once on the runner's echoed step-source line, once on the executed output line. 'contains' is therefore not the assertion; ac3 requires exactly one line ENDING with the string and discloses the echoed occurrence.
